commit.message:
rpcwallet: fail loudly when a signer node lacks its sub-servers

The remote signer client builder checked for the presence of the
walletrpc and signrpc sub-servers before it checked whether the node had
been configured to act as a remote signer at all. Because of that
ordering, a node that explicitly enabled the outbound remote signer but
was built without the signrpc and/or walletrpc build tags silently
received a NoOpClient, logged only at debug level.

The consequences were poor. The signer node started up, reported
healthy, and never dialled the watch-only node. The watch-only node was
left waiting for a signer connection that was never coming, so the
symptom appeared on a different machine from the misconfiguration, with
nothing at the default log level on either side to explain it.

Determine the missing sub-servers up front and, when the node has asked
to act as a remote signer, return an error naming them instead of
degrading to a no-op. The error also names the build tags to enable,
since a missing build tag is the root cause and an operator has no way
to infer that from a bare "sub-server unavailable" message.

Add table-driven coverage over both the configuration flag and
sub-server availability, including the previously untested case this
commit fixes. The builder had no test coverage at all before this.

commit.message:
lncfg: add WatchOnlyNode.IsSignerNode helper

Add a single predicate that answers whether the node has been configured
to act as a remote signer node, and use it in Validate.

The outbound remote signer is still gated behind an experimental flag,
but that flag is expected to go away once the feature graduates. Routing
every caller through one helper means that graduation only has to change
this function, rather than every site that happens to read
ExperimentalEnable directly.

commit.message:
sweep: track already accepted transactions

Allow already-accepted initial transactions to reach normal publication
and tracking. A publication error can follow backend acceptance, so an
identical retry must not discard the sweep claims as fatal.

Keep the shared replacement check unchanged to avoid reporting a
byte-identical fee bump as a replacement. Cover the public outcome.

Review: https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/11472
Comment: 4473647569.

sweep: retry transient mempool errors

Treat unrecognized mempool acceptance failures and reversible policy
rejections as retryable. Preserve the underlying backend error and
continue the existing fee trajectory, including an exhausted fee cap.

Keep recognized script and local initialization failures terminal.
Cover the public broadcast result and retain existing publication
failure coverage.

commit.message:
itest: add receiver-side BOLT 12 tests

Cover offer creation and decoding, and the receiver-side negotiation
loop: an invoice request arrives over an onion message and the node
replies with a signed BOLT 12 invoice carrying a blinded payment path.

lncli: add the createoffer command

Add createoffer, which calls the CreateOffer RPC of devrpc and prints the
encoded offer and its offer hash. Like the other devrpc commands, it
exists only in a dev build.

The expiry can be a duration from now, such as --expiry 1h, which lncli
converts to the absolute expiry of the offer. --absolute_expiry still
takes a timestamp, and the two flags cannot be used together.

lnd: let devrpc create offers

Add CreateOffer to the server. It builds the offer from the node's
identity, includes the active chain hash so other implementations can
validate it off mainnet, persists the offer, and returns the lno1 string
with its content-addressed offer hash.

The server gives itself to devrpc as the offer creator only when the
offer store is set.

rpcserver: move the permission setup out of addDeps

addDeps is close to the funlen limit of 200 lines. A later commit adds
the offer creator of the dev RPC to it. Move the code that adds the
macaroon permissions to the interceptor chain into addPermissions. The
behaviour does not change.

devrpc: implement CreateOffer

CreateOffer checks the request and passes it to the OfferCreator of the
config, which is nil when the node runs without BOLT 12 offers. It maps
the offer errors to gRPC codes, so that a client can tell a bad request
from a failure of the node.

devrpc: add the CreateOffer proto

Add the CreateOffer method and its messages to the Dev service, with the
POST /v2/dev/createoffer REST route. The Dev service exists only in a
dev build, so a release build has no BOLT 12 API while the feature is
experimental. The server does not implement the method yet.
